summary: Clean the M1 baseline before M2
description:
Apply the accepted 2026-07-13 full-codebase review in one M2-readiness PR, as directed by the owner. The work repairs the concurrent checkout completion race, makes every OpenAPI contract enforceable, hardens JetStream poison-message behavior and Access migrations/scanner recovery, reconciles all repository documentation with the running Go/TS system, pins executable supply-chain inputs, and completes the lower-priority resource/input/hygiene recommendations.

Conditions of Success:
- Concurrent identical checkouts can only publish and return the one persisted guest order reference; a real-PostgreSQL race test proves it
- Inventory, Commerce, Payments, and Access committed OpenAPI specs are served and checked against implementation behavior in the gate
- Permanently invalid Access events do not retry forever; transient failure behavior is bounded and observable
- TKT-44 migration-upgrade and TKT-45 scanner-recovery/corruption coverage are implemented
- PostgreSQL version authority, M1/M2 roadmap state, README, AGENTS.md, architecture, development, Docker, security, delivery, and solution-design docs agree with the actual repository
- Executable container/action inputs are pinned and dependency/security automation reflects what is actually configured
- Database/HTTP resource policies, strict JSON decoding, stale headers/generated files, and review-report tracking are cleaned up
- `make check` and the relevant race/integration tests pass; the review report marks R1-R13 complete

Source: docs/reviews/2026-07-13-code-review.md (R1-R13).

objective.note: Remove correctness, contract, documentation, supply-chain, and hygiene debt that would make M2 build on an unreliable baseline.

scope.note: In: exactly review R1-R13, including TKT-44/TKT-45. Out: TKT-43 production PSP recovery and all new M2 capability work.

uncertainties.note: Exact generator/validator choice per non-Catalog OpenAPI service and immutable image/action versions are resolved from current project tooling during planning; neither changes the accepted architecture.

dependencies.note: M1/TKT-1 is Done; no open blockers. TKT-44 and TKT-45 are incorporated follow-ups, not prerequisites.

approach.note: Apply recommendations sequentially on one branch, with a mandatory mini-plan and focused verification for each; retain the full make check gate.

first_slice.note: First executable slice is critical R1: transactional compare-and-return checkout completion plus a real-PostgreSQL race proof. Remaining accepted review items follow on the same owner-requested PR.

success.note: All 13 review checkboxes complete, duplicate follow-ups reconciled, full gate green, adversarial review clean, and documentation describes the M2-ready truth.

binding.rule: Money and ticket lifecycle trails remain append-only and pseudonymous.
Public and internal service boundaries are contract-first; committed specs must not drift from handlers.
Checkout is idempotent and recovery-aware; a completed order must expose one canonical durable outcome.
Access ticket issuance, guest capabilities, lifecycle events, and QR credentials remain Access-owned.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Readiness — READY WITH SCOPE WARNING
All seven DoR items pass and there are no blockers. The owner explicitly requested all accepted review issues in one new PR. This will exceed the normal small-review preference and touches concurrency, contracts, CI, containers, and documentation, so it is not `risk:low`; the normal plan gate applies. Implementation is sequenced recommendation-by-recommendation, starting with the approved R1 transaction/race-test plan.

Gate 1: owner prioritizes TKT-46 by moving it to Ready.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
Claimed by Codex after owner prioritized TKT-46 at Gate 1. Selection reason: M1 is complete and this accepted review cleanup is the explicit prerequisite to starting M2. Zero open blockers. Branch: `TKT-46-m2-readiness-cleanup` from `origin/main` at `3ea5878`. Not `risk:low`: concurrency, contracts, CI/containers, and broad documentation are in scope; plan gate applies.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
## Draft execution plan — TKT-46 / M2-readiness cleanup

**Branch:** `TKT-46-m2-readiness-cleanup` from `origin/main` at `3ea5878`.

### Definition of done
All R1–R13 findings in `docs/reviews/2026-07-13-code-review.md` are implemented and checked off; TKT-44/TKT-45 are reconciled as incorporated work; the full gate and focused PostgreSQL/race tests pass; docs describe the actual M2-ready Go/TS system; one PR carries a risk-ordered review guide.

### Test seams
- **Primary seam:** existing isolated Compose smoke stack (`scripts/smoke.sh`) because the highest-risk findings are PostgreSQL concurrency, migrations, service contracts, and JetStream behavior.
- **Focused seams:** Go/TS package tests for permanent/transient event classification, strict decoding, QR corruption, scanner recovery, and resource configuration.
- **Gate seam:** existing `make check`, extended only where the review found missing enforceability. No parallel bespoke harness.

### Work units (risk order)

1. **R1 — canonical checkout completion.** Add a Commerce store operation that locks the order, atomically returns either the newly persisted or existing `guest_order_ref`, verifies affected rows, and never lets the caller publish a local/unpersisted value. Add a `smoke`-tagged real-PostgreSQL concurrency test in the Commerce module and run it from `scripts/smoke.sh`; update the handler to publish only the returned reference.

2. **R2 — enforce all OpenAPI contracts.** Embed and serve Commerce/Payments specs like Catalog/Inventory/Access; add shared kin-openapi request validation without making internal endpoints public; add smoke contract checks that load/validate every served spec and validate representative responses; extend deterministic generated-artifact drift checks where generated types are consumed. Preserve gateway denial of `/internal/` routes.

3. **R3 — JetStream poison-message policy.** Introduce typed permanent event-validation errors in Access. Publish permanently rejected identifier-only events to a dedicated failed-event subject before `Term`; bound transient deliveries/backoff; count permanent/transient failures with OTel metrics; unit-test unsupported schema/invalid identifiers/transient classification. Keep delivery retry idempotent.

4. **R4/R5 — incorporated follow-ups.** Add a `smoke`-tagged Access migration upgrade test (0001 data → 0002 → history readable + redeemable). Catch asynchronous `BarcodeDetector.detect()` failures, stop tracks, return the operator to paste mode, and test it. Replace base64url-last-character mutation with deterministic signature-byte corruption.

5. **R10/R11 — operational and input policy.** Record ADR-013 for shared runtime resource/input policy; add small shared helpers for bounded DB pools, HTTP server timeouts, and strict one-document JSON decoding; wire all services/gateway; document environment defaults; add focused tests. Do not introduce runtime/deployment architecture changes.

6. **R9 — reproducibility/security automation.** Resolve current official image versions/digests and GitHub Action commit SHAs from primary sources; pin executable inputs; add Dependabot coverage for Go workspaces, pnpm, Docker, and Actions; add a scheduled/PR security workflow for govulncheck, pnpm audit, and container/config scanning without putting network advisory lookups into the deterministic local gate.

7. **R6–R8 — documentation authority.** Keep PostgreSQL 18.4 as the accepted/current stack (ADR-007 + running Compose) and correct AGENTS.md. Mark M1 complete/M2 next; update README, architecture/event-flow diagram, development, Docker, and configuration. Replace or sharply trim Python/FastAPI/Jira/Confluence template guidance so every indexed document applies to this repository.

8. **R12/R13 — hygiene and review trace.** Fix stale service headers; untrack ignored Astro-generated files; track/link the dated review report; check off each completed recommendation immediately after its focused verification.

9. **Final verification/hand-off.** Run focused smoke-tagged PostgreSQL tests, `go test -race` for local modules, `make check`, and any deterministic config validation. Commit/push, open a TKT-46 PR, run the mandatory adversarial Codex diff review, triage every finding, re-green, then post the risk-ordered review guide and stop at Gate 3.

### Improvement-workflow sequencing
The accepted review executor requires each R-item to retain its own mini plan/approval and focused verification. The approved R1 mini-plan is Work Unit 1. Subsequent R-items will be presented at their mandatory mini-gate before edits, while remaining on this one owner-requested branch/PR.

### Pre-mortem (lens: pre-mortem)
1. **PR becomes unreviewable.** Mitigation: risk-ordered work units, focused commits, review checkbox updated per unit, final walkthrough by concern rather than filename.
2. **Contract middleware exposes or validates the wrong surface.** Mitigation: mount validators inside services, retain gateway internal-route denial, and smoke both public specs and 404 internal paths.
3. **Supply-chain “pinning” breaks latest-stable policy or local reproducibility.** Mitigation: record resolution date/source, pin digests/SHAs, let Dependabot propose updates, keep advisory-network scans outside `make check`.
4. **Shared helpers become an accidental framework.** Mitigation: ADR-013 limits them to DB pool/server defaults and strict decoding; no domain abstractions.
5. **Migration/concurrency tests only pass in CI-specific timing.** Mitigation: exercise store transactions directly against the already-isolated smoke PostgreSQL, using barriers/locks rather than sleeps.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan-final -->
## Final plan — TKT-46 M2 readiness cleanup

### Definition of done

- Resolve every finding R1–R13 in `docs/reviews/2026-07-13-code-review.md`; a rejected/already-satisfied sub-finding is documented rather than forced into a meaningless diff.
- Preserve the M1 behavior and service boundaries, reconcile TKT-44/TKT-45 without duplicate future work, and keep `make check` green.
- Deliver the cleanup as one reviewable PR from `TKT-46-m2-readiness-cleanup`.
- Follow the review executor literally: R1→R9, then R10→R13, one recommendation at a time. Each recommendation gets its own analysis, mini-plan, explicit B3 approval, tests-first change, focused verification, checkbox update, and continue/stop prompt. R1's mini-plan is already approved; Gate 2 approves entering Building, not the later R2–R13 mini-plans.

### Test seam and execution order

The primary end-to-end seam remains the Compose smoke suite. Deterministic store/migration tests and real PostgreSQL/NATS integration tests cover concurrency and infrastructure behavior that black-box timing alone cannot prove. Unit/table tests cover strict decoding, configuration, and UI failure states.

1. **R1 — canonical concurrent checkout completion (critical).** Move completion into a Commerce store transaction that locks the order, reuses or persists the canonical `guest_order_ref`, checks affected rows, and returns only committed state. Add a deterministic PostgreSQL concurrency test. Strengthen the existing smoke race test so every successful identical checkout returns the same durable reference and that reference retrieves the expected Access ticket bundle; do not accept an unexplained loser reference.
2. **R2 — enforce all non-Catalog OpenAPI contracts.** First complete Inventory, Commerce, Payments, and Access specs with request, success, and material error schemas for every operation/status family. Embed and serve each spec. Add deterministic generated operation/types or an equivalent checked-in operation/schema coverage artifact for all four services, with `make generate`/drift checks. Apply kin-openapi request validation and response-conformance tests across every operation/status family. Test direct service contracts plus gateway routing, including generic `/internal/` denial and denial of Inventory confirm/finalize/release routes.
3. **R3 — terminate poison events safely.** Define typed permanent/transient consumer failures; publish a sanitized, versioned failure record (identifiers + bounded reason code, no original hostile body) before `Term` on permanent failures. Configure finite `MaxDeliver` and JetStream `BackOff`, removing fixed-delay NAK behavior that bypasses it. Define exhausted-transient handling through a terminal advisory/failure record, low-cardinality OTel counters, and an operator replay note. Add a real-NATS test for permanent failure publication-before-termination, failed-publication redelivery, bounded transient attempts, durable consumer config, terminal exhaustion, and metric export; retain focused classification tests.
4. **R4 — prove Access forward migration.** Add a smoke-tagged migration test that creates a disposable database, applies only 0001 through an exposed testable migration provider, seeds issued/delivered history, applies 0002, verifies preservation plus redeemed support, then drops the database. It must not reuse the already-fully-migrated Access service database.
5. **R5 — scanner resilience and deterministic tamper proof.** Catch asynchronous detector rejection inside the frame loop, stop tracks/frame scheduling, and show a useful fallback while paste remains usable. Add the rejected-detect UI test. Replace probabilistic token mutation with deterministic signed-byte tampering and assert the modified token actually differs.
6. **R6 — PostgreSQL authority.** Standardize the repository on PostgreSQL 18.4 (matching Compose and ADR-007), update AGENTS/README/architecture/conventions, and add a lightweight drift assertion over authoritative references.
7. **R7 — current M1 documentation.** Reconcile README, ROADMAP, architecture, testing, and relevant product docs with the completed M1 stack, commands, gateway surface, and actual milestone state. Validate links and commands used by a clean clone.
8. **R8 — remove obsolete scaffold guidance.** Delete or rewrite Python/Jira/Confluence/release/deploy template claims that do not describe this repo; keep reusable generic conventions only when accurate for the Go/TS/local-board project. Search for stale terms and repair inbound links.
9. **R9 — pin and continuously audit executable inputs.** Inventory and pin every Compose image and every normal/smoke Dockerfile base by immutable digest, plus GitHub Actions by full commit SHA; document the human-readable version beside pins. Add Dependabot entries for all eight Go module directories, the root pnpm workspace, Docker surfaces, and GitHub Actions. Add pinned security tooling with explicit failure policy: Go vulnerability scan across all modules, pnpm audit threshold, secret/config scan targets, and container-image or filesystem scanning with documented scope. Newly added scanner actions/binaries/containers are pinned too; CI and local documentation identify what is enforced where.
10. **R10 — bounded runtime resources.** Inventory every `sql.Open` path (including Payments verification/recovery paths) and every HTTP server; the gateway gets HTTP policy only. Introduce exact env-backed defaults and validation for max-open, max-idle, connection lifetime, idle lifetime, read-header/read/write/idle timeouts, and graceful shutdown. Reject invalid/negative settings at startup. Add config tests and focused lifecycle tests without over-generalizing service bootstraps.
11. **R11 — strict bounded JSON at public write endpoints.** Apply one shared decoder policy only to Commerce, Payments, Inventory, and Access JSON write handlers: body size cap, unknown-field rejection, exactly one JSON value, empty-body handling, and whitespace after the sole value. Preserve endpoint/domain status semantics (including Access credential `422` where applicable). Table-test unknown fields, second documents, empty/oversized bodies, valid trailing whitespace, and normal requests. The gateway is out of scope because it does not decode these bodies.
12. **R12 — stale hygiene only.** Treat the Astro “untrack” sub-finding as already satisfied/rejected because `.astro` is ignored and absent from git at the review base. Fix genuinely stale generated headers/comments and verify ignored generated state stays absent from `git ls-files`.
13. **R13 — retain review evidence.** Stop ignoring `docs/reviews/`, add the review report to the PR, and document the review-report lifecycle/checklist convention.

### Ticket reconciliation and delivery

- TKT-44 maps to R4 and TKT-45 maps to R5. Link/comment them as incorporated by TKT-46 now, but do not mark them Done before the TKT-46 PR merges; close them with metrics during the TKT-46 closeout so they cannot be implemented twice.
- After R13: run focused race tests where applicable, the full `make check`, and a clean-worktree/ignored-file audit; commit, push, and open a TKT-46 PR. Run the mandatory read-only Codex diff review, fix blocking findings, rebase/re-green, post the PR review guide, then stop at Gate 3.

### Pre-mortem controls

- **Large PR hides regressions:** keep one commit/work unit per R-item where practical and record focused test evidence after each.
- **Schema middleware creates false confidence:** schemas become contract-complete before conformance middleware is credited.
- **Infrastructure tests flake:** isolate databases/consumers with unique names, bounded polling, and deterministic cleanup; never rely on sleeps for correctness.
- **Security automation adds new floating inputs:** pin every introduced executable input in the same change and state failure thresholds.
- **Shared helpers become a framework:** extract only policies repeated across current call sites; retain service-specific bootstraps and status semantics.

### Review lens

Adversarial feasibility/coverage review applied. It strengthened R1 end-to-end proof, required schema completeness for R2, real JetStream semantics for R3, disposable migration isolation for R4, exhaustive R9/R10 surfaces, strict executor ordering, explicit TKT-44/45 lifecycle handling, and corrected the false Astro tracking claim.
